title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the unpublished continuation (pp. 650bis-787) of 'La Longue Marche'. Notation: U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,infinity}, with S_3 acting by permuting the three cusps. T^0 = G_m^{0,1,inf}/G_m(diagonal) = G_m tensor_Z M, where M = Z^3/Z(diagonal), a rank-2 lattice carrying the S_3 action. T^0 is exactly the connected generalized Jacobian J^0 of P^1 with modulus (0)+(1)+(inf).

Input from the previous page. Equivariant cohomology is computed with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence H^p(S_3, H^q(S, T^0)) => H^{p+q}(S, S_3; T^0). Two facts feed in:
- H^0(S_3, M tensor I) = H^1(S_3, M tensor I) = 0 for every abelian group I (formula 309).
- H^1(S, T^0) = Pic(S) tensor M.
Together they give H^0(S, S_3; T^0) = H^1(S, S_3; T^0) = 0 for every scheme S (formula 310).

Proposition. Every (S_3 semidirect T^0)-torsor over an arbitrary base S has a unique rigidification, i.e. a unique S_3-invariant section.
- Existence follows from H^1(S, S_3; T^0) = 0.
- Uniqueness follows from H^0(S, S_3; T^0) = H^0(S_3, T^0(S)) = 0.

Corollary. Over any S there is a unique S_3-equivariant morphism phi: U_{0,3,S} -> T^0_S whose 'linear part' is the identity. Precisely: via the universal property of generalized Jacobians, phi factors through J^*_S -> J^0_S, and the induced map J^0 -> J^0 must be the identity.
- Proof idea: the degree-1 component J^1 of the generalized Jacobian is an S_3-equivariant T^0-torsor. The Proposition gives it a canonical invariant point, so J^1 is canonically identified with T^0, and phi is the Abel-Jacobi map.

The NB makes phi explicit. U_{0,3} is identified with U_1 = {(x_0, x_1, x_inf) mod diagonal G_m : x_0 + x_1 + x_inf = 0}, the line x_0 + x_1 + x_2 = 0 in P^2 minus the coordinate lines. In coordinates t -> (t : 1-t : -1), which is the S_3-symmetric form of the unit equation x + y = 1. Direct check: the naive Abel-Jacobi map is t -> (t, 1-t, 1) up to translation. The invariant section fixes the translation by the sign (1, 1, -1), making the embedding S_3-equivariant.

Corollary 3 (begun here, continued on the next page) is the twisted form. Take a Brauer-Severi curve Y/S (a form of P^1) with an etale degree-3 closed subscheme S'. Then U = Y - S' has a canonical Aut(Y,S')-equivariant map U -> J^0_{U/S} = G_m tensor M(S'/S). Here M(S'/S) is p_*Z_{S'}/Z_S, the lattice M twisted by the S_3-torsor attached to S'. So J^0 is the torus R_{S'/S}G_m / G_m.

Purpose in the manuscript: to have canonical, descent-compatible, S_3-equivariant 'Albanese' embeddings of the tripod and of all its twisted forms. These serve the study of the Galois/Teichmuller action on fundamental groups of M_{0,n}, in particular how the torus quotient interacts with automorphisms.
errors: No mathematical error found. The key vanishing claims check out. For M = Z^3/Z: invariants vanish, since the transposition (01) forces a = b and similarly for the other pairs. H^1(S_3, M tensor I) = 0 follows from 0 -> I -> I^3 -> M tensor I -> 0 together with Shapiro's lemma: H^1(S_3, I) -> H^1(S_2, I) is an isomorphism, and H^2(S_3, I) -> H^2(S_2, I) is injective because the 3-primary part H^2(C_3, I)^{S_2} = (I/3)^{(-1)} = 0.

Minor imprecision: '(S_3.T^0)-torseur' should be read as an S_3-equivariant T^0-torsor on S with trivial S_3 action on S (equivalently, an extension compatible with the semidirect product). The statement is correct under that reading.

In the corollary, the symbols written \hat T^*_S -> T_S denote the generalized Jacobian J^*_S -> J^0_S; this is notational inconsistency, not a mathematical error. The previous page's formula (310) also writes H^0(S_3, S_3; ...) where H^0(S, S_3; ...) is meant.

ideas.what: Vanishing of H^0 and H^1 of S_3 with coefficients in M tensor I for every abelian group I, giving rigidity (unique invariant sections) of S_3-equivariant T^0-torsors over any base
ideas.modern_name: equivariant cohomology vanishing / rigidification of equivariant torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group cohomology (Shapiro's lemma); no specific attribution
ideas.where_published: Possibly analogous rigidification arguments in La Longue Marche (Malgoire ed.), first part; this portion is unpublished

ideas.what: Canonical S_3-equivariant Abel-Jacobi embedding of P^1-{0,1,inf} into the 2-torus G_m^3/G_m, explicitly as the line x0+x1+x_inf=0
ideas.modern_name: generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht-Serre) Albanese map of the tripod; unit-equation embedding
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht, Serre (Groupes algebriques et corps de classes); the symmetric unit-equation line is classical
ideas.where_published: Not in the published part of La Longue Marche as far as known

ideas.what: Twisted version: for a form Y of P^1 with an etale cubic S', a canonical Aut(Y,S')-equivariant map Y-S' -> R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m = G_m tensor M(S'/S)
ideas.modern_name: descent of the generalized-Jacobian embedding for twisted forms of M_{0,4}-type tripods; norm-torus embedding of twisted P^1 minus 3 points
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / implicit in work on twisted unit equations and Chabauty with generalized Jacobians
ideas.where_published: unpublished continuation (next page of this manuscript)

missed.claim: A clean base-free statement: twisted forms of the tripod over an arbitrary base S (a conic with an etale degree-3 divisor) carry a unique equivariant embedding into the twisted torus G_m tensor M(S'/S). Uniqueness is guaranteed by the vanishing of H^0 and H^1 of S_3 with coefficients in M tensor I for every I. This is a small but neat canonical-rigidification result not explicitly stated in standard references.
missed.quote: il existe une unique rigidification de celui-ci, i.e. une unique section, invariante par les opérations de S_3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical equivariant torus embeddings of twisted P^1-{0,1,inf} are used in descent and Chabauty-Kim style analyses of S-unit equations over general bases. Here a canonical base-change-compatible choice is guaranteed. Mildly useful, but essentially folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a correct, careful, but essentially routine rigidification argument via S_3-cohomology. The resulting canonical equivariant embedding of P^1-{0,1,inf} into G_m^2 is classical. The only mildly notable feature is the formulation over arbitrary bases, including twisted forms, inside the unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche.
